wins.label: Record Data Center Revenue
wins.evidence: Revenue coming in above expectations, driven by record Instinct and EPYC product sales and robust demand for our Ryzen PC processors.

wins.label: EPYC CPU Share Gain
wins.evidence: We gained server CPU share in the quarter as enterprise wins accelerated.

wins.label: Cloud Provider Adoption of EPYC
wins.evidence: Cloud providers expanded their use of EPYC CPUs across their infrastructure, and we began the initial ramp of fifth-gen EPYC processors.

wins.label: Cloudflare Genoa-X Adoption
wins.evidence: Cloudflare selected Genoa-X processors with our industry-leading 3D chiplet stacking technology to power their next-generation servers that support twice as many requests per second and deliver 60% higher performance per watt versus their prior generation.

wins.label: EPYC Instance Adoption
wins.evidence: Public cloud instances increased 20% year-over-year to more than 950 as Microsoft, AWS and others launched or expanded their EPYC processor-powered offerings in the quarter. EPYC instance adoption with enterprise customers also grew in the quarter, highlighted by wins with Adobe, Boeing, Micron Nestle, Slack, Synopsys, Tata and others.

risks.label: Gaming Segment Decline
risks.evidence: Semi-custom sales declined as Microsoft and Sony reduced channel inventory.

risks.label: Embedded Segment Recovery
risks.evidence: Embedded demand continues recovering gradually, led by strength in test and emulation offset by ongoing softness in the industrial market.

risks.label: Market Competition (GPU)
risks.evidence: If you remember, Harsh, our EPYC ramp from Zen 1, Zen 2, Zen 3, Zen 4 we had extremely good product even back in the Rome days, but it does take time to ensure that there is trust built, there is familiarity with the product set.

risks.label: PC Market Seasonality
risks.evidence: I would expect there will be seasonality going into the first half. That's typical in our business.

risks.label: Supply Chain Constraints
risks.evidence: Inventory increased sequentially by $383 million to $5.4 billion, primarily to support the continued ramp of Data Center segment products.
